title: Zariski log structures, charts and association to the etale site
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. A Zariski prelog structure on $X$ consists of a sheaf of commutative monoids $N$ on its Zariski site [def-sc-zariski-site] and a monoid-sheaf morphism $\alpha:N\to(\mathcal O_X,\cdot)$. Its stalk at $x$ is the filtered colimit of $N(U)$ over open neighborhoods of $x$, and $\alpha_x$ is induced by the actual ring germs. A Zariski log structure is such a prelog structure for which, at every point, $\alpha_x$ reflects units and induces a bijection $N_x^\times\to\mathcal O_{X,x}^\times$; this is precisely the stalkwise inverse-image-of-units isomorphism axiom of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], on the Zariski site. Write $u_x:\mathcal O_{X,x}^\times\to N_x$ for the inverse unit identification followed by inclusion. For an open $U$ and a commutative monoid $P$, a homomorphism $h:P\to N(U)$ is a chart if for each $x\in U$ the map $P\times\mathcal O_{X,x}^\times\to N_x$, $(p,a)\mapsto h_x(p)u_x(a)$, is surjective and its kernel congruence is generated by $(p,1)\sim(1,a)$ whenever $\alpha_xh_x(p)=a$. Equivalently the log structure associated to the prescribed prelog map $\alpha h$ is $N|_U$.

For an etale log structure $M$ on $X$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], a map from $N$ to $M$ in adjoint form is a family $e_U:N(U)\to M(U\hookrightarrow X)$ of monoid homomorphisms, natural under inclusions of opens, such that $\alpha_M e_U$ is $\alpha_N$ under the canonical identification $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)=\mathcal O_X(U)$. Such a map exhibits $M$ as the associated etale log structure of $N$ if for every etale log structure $K$ and every compatible natural family $c_U:N(U)\to K(U\hookrightarrow X)$ there is a unique log homomorphism $f:M\to K$ over the identity, that is, a homomorphism of monoid sheaves with $\alpha_K f=\alpha_M$ (a morphism of log structures as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] whose underlying scheme map is the identity), with $f_Ue_U=c_U$ for every $U$. This universal property is the inverse-image adjunction followed by associated-log formation; it specifies both the associated log structure and the canonical map up to unique isomorphism.
